verdict.rationale: Omarchy's own docs show a first-party agent integration: a default agent is set up on first boot to work on the computer, crash notifications hand off to the agent, bundled skills let users describe the apps or themes they want, and the omarchy CLI is positioned for agents doing customization and configuration. Natural-language operation therefore comes through bundled third-party agent harnesses (OpenCode, Claude Code), not a native NL command layer. Voxtype dictation only inserts text and is not command control. missing for 10: a native natural-language command interface for the OS itself, documentation of how far agent-driven system operation extends, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: On first boot, Omarchy invites you to set up a default agent. Pick your favorite, sign in, and put it to work on your computer.
Omarchy ships with skills to help your agent make apps, plugins, and themes. Describe what you want, try what it builds, and share it with everyone.
When an app crashes, click the notification to send your agent on the case.
you can also control it through the `omarchy` CLI. This is particularly helpful when you're having an AI agent work with you on customization or configuration.
